modules.name: Module 30 — Real Payment Provider Integration, Razorpay India (Test Mode First), Payment Attempts, Provider Orders, Secure Web + Android Provider Handoff, Server-Side Verification, Webhooks, Idempotency, Payment Recovery & Reconciliation
modules.scope: Owner spec 2026-10-07: the real payment domain behind the Module 12 payment step. A confirmed backend checkout (Module 29) is paid through a PAYMENT ATTEMPT: the backend creates it for exactly the checkout's total and currency, creates ONE provider order for it, and hands the client only what the provider's own interface needs (a public key id and an order reference). What that interface tells the browser or the app is REPORTED to the backend; the backend verifies it with the provider. VERIFIED = the provider reports a captured payment on this attempt's own order for this attempt's amount and currency — never a client's word, a client signature alone or a webhook's content alone. Provider interface with a Razorpay client (HTTP, per the documentation reviewed on 2026-10-07) and a development provider; payment state machine with pending, unknown and review states; webhooks (raw-body signature, deduplication, queue); reconciliation with a scheduled sweep and late-success rules; idempotency and duplicate protection enforced by the database; checkout and pickup hold kept for as long as paying takes; verified payment / order separation (ORDER_PENDING, RECOVERY_REQUIRED); customer API, admin API with "ask the provider again" as the only action; Customer Web payment page, Android payment screen, admin Payments page and System card on the backend. NOT in scope and NOT built: order creation (Module 31), refunds, settlements, saved cards / tokens, cash at pickup (not approved), iOS, live mode. STATUS: PARTIAL — the payment domain is COMPLETE locally with the development provider; RAZORPAY TEST MODE = PENDING PROVIDER CONFIGURATION (no credentials on this machine: real provider E2E on web and Android, and a provider-delivered webhook, are not done). LOCAL only; production NOT touched; no real money; live mode refused in code. No Razorpay credentials exist on the development machine: the real Razorpay API, Razorpay's own checkout and a webhook sent by Razorpay were NOT exercised. Owner approval of Modules 24–29 is still pending in words (CF-399).

modules.name: Module 31 — Order Creation, Immutable Order Snapshot, Payment → Order Orchestration, Zero-Total Order Path, Order Number, Restaurant Order Workflow, Customer Order Confirmation, Failure Compensation / Recovery
modules.scope: Owner spec 2026-10-07: the order domain behind the paid checkout. An order is created by the BACKEND from a VERIFIED payment attempt (PaymentVerified → queue → OrderFulfillmentService) — or, for a confirmed checkout with nothing to pay, at the customer's request — never from a client's word. Exactly once (one locked fulfilment record per checkout, one order per checkout and per payment, database-enforced). The order is an IMMUTABLE copy of the confirmed checkout: items, options, prices, promotion, taxes, fees, total, pickup, restaurant, customer, legal references, a safe payment reference. Order numbers FOTG-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX. Status machine WAITING_FOR_RESTAURANT → ACCEPTED → PREPARING → READY_FOR_PICKUP (→ PICKED_UP → COMPLETED in Module 32), REJECTED with a structured reason, CANCELLED by administrators; money state apart (payment_state, refund_status: REQUIRED on a paid rejection / cancellation). The pickup hold becomes the order's reservation (or the slot is taken again, atomically); promotion use redeemed; checkout, cart and pickup selection CONVERTED. Payment VERIFIED, order NOT CREATED is represented, retried with backoff, swept every minute, surfaced to administrators and recoverable by hand (admin.orders.recover, audited). Pickup credential foundation (opaque token hashed, encrypted code). Restaurant API (queue, accept, reject, start preparing, ready; version conflicts; idempotent), customer API (list, detail by number, zero-total fulfil), admin API (list, detail, cancel, fulfilments, recover, numbers). Customer Web, Restaurant Dashboard, Platform Admin and Android run on it. NOT in scope and NOT built: realtime tracking (polling until Module 32), secure pickup verification and PICKED_UP, refund processing, notification delivery, customer cancellation, delay reporting. STATUS: COMPLETE (local) — order creation, order snapshot, restaurant order workflow and payment → order recovery complete locally with the development payment provider; REALTIME TRACKING, SECURE PICKUP VERIFICATION, REFUND PROCESSING, NOTIFICATION DELIVERY = NOT COMPLETE (later modules); PRODUCTION = NO. LOCAL only; production NOT touched; no real money (the development provider). Razorpay itself is still PENDING PROVIDER CONFIGURATION (Module 30). Owner approval of Modules 24–30 is still pending in words (CF-422); the Module 31 start condition "Module 30 approved" was answered by the owner's choice to start Module 31 with Module 30 PARTIAL (provider configuration gap only).

modules.name: Module 32 — Realtime Order Tracking, Order Event Stream, WebSocket / SSE / Polling Fallback, Customer Live Order Status, Restaurant Live Order Queue, Secure Pickup QR / Manual Code, Single-Use Pickup Verification, Picked-Up Transition, Order Completion
modules.scope: Owner spec 2026-10-08: the realtime layer and the end of the order. Every order change writes a numbered timeline line and, after its commit, a NOTICE (version, event sequence, state — never the order) on two private channels over Laravel Reverb: customer.order.{order id} (the owner) and restaurant.location.{location id} (staff with orders.view), authorized on the server with the API's bearer tokens; clients compare version / sequence, ignore what is not newer, read the order again on a gap, a reconnection, a tab resume or an app resume, and poll when the socket is away (REST stays primary; SSE optional, not built). An event stream API (cursor = after_sequence) is the resync. The pickup credential is high-entropy and opaque (FOTG1. + 256 random bits, encrypted at rest with its hash; a six-character code bound to the order), one ACTIVE per order, rotatable by the customer, expiring 24 h after the pickup time; verification (POST /restaurant/pickup/verify, restaurant.pickup.verify at the order's location = the scanner's location, order READY) is one transaction under the order's and the credential's locks: consume exactly once, READY_FOR_PICKUP → PICKED_UP, then COMPLETED by OrderCompletionService in its own transaction (job + sweep as the nets). Replays, wrong restaurant / location, not-ready, rejected / cancelled, expired, revoked, wrong codes (counted, locked), rate limits per staff member / location — every attempt recorded without the secret. Customer Web (Echo), Restaurant Dashboard (live queue, camera / hardware scanner / manual code), Android (Pusher-protocol client), Platform Admin (pickup audit, Realtime and pickup numbers). STATUS: COMPLETE (local) — realtime tracking, the event stream, the live restaurant queue, secure pickup QR / manual code, single-use verification, PICKED_UP and COMPLETED complete locally with Laravel Reverb and the development payment provider; BACKGROUND PUSH, REFUND PROCESSING, REVIEWS NOT COMPLETE (later modules); PRODUCTION = NO. LOCAL only; production NOT touched; no real money (the development provider). Razorpay itself is still PENDING PROVIDER CONFIGURATION (Module 30). modules.name: Module 33 — Notification Delivery Backend, Customer Device Registration, Firebase Cloud Messaging (Android), In-App Notification Center, Order / Pickup Event Notifications, Email + SMS Provider Abstractions, Customer Preference Enforcement, Delivery Attempts, Retries / Dead Letter / Invalid Token Cleanup
modules.scope: Owner spec 2026-10-09: the notification domain. A domain event (an order step of Module 31 / 32, a security event of Module 21 / 25) becomes ONE logical notification per customer and type (dedupe key) with one delivery per channel — and per device for push — written after the commit and sent by a queue worker; the policy reads the Module 25 preference matrix, the platform channel configuration, the customer status and the destinations; the development push provider answers locally (FCM HTTP v1 implemented with the official google/auth library, REAL FCM = PENDING FIREBASE CONFIGURATION); e-mail goes to the local mailer (REAL EMAIL PROVIDER = PENDING); SMS is off (REAL SMS PROVIDER = PENDING). ASAP = now + preparation + restaurant buffer (restaurant data); open-but-not-accepting blocks pickup distinctly from closed; closed restaurants offer scheduled pickup only.

Client payment success is not order confirmation; backend verification (signature / status / webhooks) is mandatory later; order confirmation and restaurant notification occur only after that verification.

Payment initiation must be idempotent (client guard + backend idempotency + verified, idempotent webhooks); an unknown payment status must never trigger an immediate duplicate payment — the customer checks the status first.
Payment secrets never belong in Web / Android code, public env files or git; mock verification is development-only and must be impossible in production builds.

OTP delivery: the code is generated and verified by FoodOnTheGo; SMS providers are interchangeable drivers (MSG91, 2Factor, Twilio) selected by configuration with an optional fallback. OTP delivery order (owner asked for the best recommendation, 2026-09-30): Truecaller one-tap on Android (free) → WhatsApp authentication message → SMS (MSG91, 2Factor backup). A resend moves to the next channel. Locally nothing is sent.

India is the first ACTIVE market; the market architecture stays global-ready (a market, its regions, cities, coverage and features are data). Country = ISO 3166-1, currency = ISO 4217, time zone = IANA. India: INR, en-IN, Asia/Kolkata, metric.

Market availability is backend-authoritative: market → region → city → service area, a child never more available than its parent. A city existing does not imply coverage; service areas define operational availability; route corridors represent operational route coverage.

WGS84 / SRID 4326 is the spatial standard; PostGIS is authoritative for geographic queries; spatial columns use GiST; geometry is exchanged as GeoJSON ([longitude, latitude]). Invalid geometry is rejected, never repaired.
Service areas may overlap (priority, then the smaller area); a point on a boundary is inside. Only ACTIVE areas inside their effective dates serve customers; TESTING is internal.

Customer APIs never expose draft / future markets or internal fields. Admin APIs may show them according to permission and market scope. Every admin market change is authorised by the backend, needs the version it edited, a reason when service is taken away, and is audited.

Restaurant locations connect to this geography in Module 23; journey route discovery uses it later. No Google Routes / Places integration exists in Module 22. Development geographic fixtures are not business launch commitments.

Module 22 result: MODULE 23 MAY START = YES. Market backend, geography backend and PostGIS foundation = COMPLETE (local). Restaurant backend = NOT COMPLETE. Journey routing = NOT COMPLETE. PRODUCTION = NO.

Organization and location are separate rows with independent administrative statuses; a customer "restaurant" is a location. An organization that is not approved hides all its locations; one location can be suspended alone.
Location slug is unique per market (not globally); the public UUID is the API id; integer ids stay internal.

service_area_id is a stored association (index for lists) resolved by PostGIS on create / move and re-resolved on geography changes; visibility and orderability are decided from the geometry per request.

Visible to customers = organization and location APPROVED + market serving + point inside a public service area (ACTIVE or PAUSED area, public city and region). Orderable = visible + area / city / region serving + not temporarily closed + pickup offered + accepting + open now. The first failing condition is the reason.
Customers get AREA_UNAVAILABLE for every geography pause and a plain 404 for anything hidden; staff and administrators see the full reason.

Reading hours and pickup settings = restaurant.profile.view; profile = restaurant.profile.manage; hours = restaurant.hours.manage; pickup settings = restaurant.pickup_settings.manage; accepting switch and temporary closure = restaurant.settings.manage.
Staff changes need restaurant.staff.manage across the whole organization; a location-limited manager may read staff who share a location but not change them.
Memberships are the source of truth; RBAC role assignments are derived from them (organization scope for all locations, one assignment per location otherwise) and refreshed on every change.
404 for a restaurant that is not one of the caller's ACTIVE memberships, 403 for a missing permission at a restaurant that is — nothing reveals which restaurants exist.
Final-owner rule is defined in permission terms: the last ACTIVE member who may manage staff across all locations cannot be removed, suspended or demoted.
Nobody changes or revokes their own membership; nobody grants a role or access that may do more than they may (compared permission by permission).

Suspending a membership removes access at once but does not end the person's FoodOnTheGo session; revoking ends their sessions when it was their only restaurant. Revoked rows stay for history and can be re-invited.
Administrators invite the first owner of an organization; self-service partner onboarding is out of scope.
Special hours have no version (one row per date; the last write wins); the accepting switch has no version (the last request wins); profile, hours and pickup settings carry their own versions.
Restaurant list and detail are not cached server-side; only the cuisine taxonomy is cached and flushed on every restaurant / market write.
Default location of the dashboard = the first APPROVED location by creation order, else the oldest location (documented in the context endpoint).

Rejecting needs a category and an explanation for the restaurant; rejecting, suspending and deactivating need an internal reason. The explanation is shown in the dashboard only while the status it explains is current.
Only COUNTER pickup can be enabled in India today (market pickup rules); CURBSIDE and DRIVE_THROUGH are offered as disabled with "Not available in this market yet".

Ratings and review counts in API mode are development figures where the fixtures have them and "No reviews yet" otherwise — no reviews backend exists; marketing illustrations (home hero, how it works) keep sample fixtures.
Menus stay development data keyed by the existing restaurant id (matched by slug); a backend restaurant the fixtures do not know shows "menu unavailable" until Module 24.
Images are metadata only (type, URL, alt text, order); upload and object storage are a later module (CF-319). The Android app loads only absolute image URLs.

Verification documents, "request information", restaurant-side submission, an admin screen for creating organizations / locations / the first owner, and a taxonomy admin API are carry-forwards (CF-318, CF-321, CF-322, CF-323).

Both customer apps recompute "open now" from the backend hours with the backend's own schedule rules (period belongs to the date it opens, closes <= opens runs overnight, equal = 24 h, special dates replace, back-to-back periods join) and never from fixtures.
Pagination links follow the project convention (page[number] / page[size] with the request's filters) on every list — the framework default (?page=N) was a bug (BUG-110).
Public restaurant endpoints use the search rate limit (configurable; local 600 / min); staff and admin writes use the admin-sensitive limit; invitation accept uses the password-reset limit.
The admin header badge states per section whether data comes from the backend; dashboard sections still on development data carry a "Demo data" label — nothing is presented as live when it is not.
Timestamps in the API are ISO-8601 UTC; wall-clock opening times are in the location time zone. Money does not appear in this module; integer minor units remain the rule.
Module 23 result: MODULE 24 MAY START = YES. Restaurant core backend = COMPLETE (local). Menu / order / payment backend = NOT COMPLETE. PRODUCTION = NO.
Owner approved Module 23 (chat, 2026-10-03): "Module 23 approved". Device verification of APK build027 and the browser reviews (TE-208) remain separate owner items until confirmed.
Menu is location-scoped: one menu per restaurant location, created on first use (ACTIVE, "Menu"); the model allows more menus per location, V1 uses one.
Customer Web, Android, the Restaurant Dashboard and the admin use the same backend menu domain (one set of tables, services and documents).
Menu currency is explicit ISO 4217 and equals the currency of the location; a client never sends a currency.
India menu currency is INR; prices are paise (integer minor units).
Money uses integer minor units everywhere (no decimals, no floats); the limits are configuration, not code.
Frontend-submitted prices are never authoritative: unit_price_minor / price in a request are refused (422); the backend quotes and will charge.
Menu categories use an explicit display_order; reorder is one permutation of all non-archived categories (all or nothing).
Menu items have stable public UUIDs and per-menu slugs created once from the name, changed only by an explicit slug field.
Item status differentiates SOLD_OUT, TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE (visible, not orderable), DISABLED (hidden) and ARCHIVED (hidden, final).
Variants are generic data (Size, Portion, Crust …), never hardcoded as Size.
Modifiers are generic data (Add-ons, Spice level, Remove ingredients …).
Min / max selection rules are validated by the backend on write and again when pricing.
Required groups cannot be impossible to satisfy: a required group needs at least one available option, and an item whose required group lost its options is not orderable (REQUIRED_GROUP_UNAVAILABLE).
Option price adjustments use the item / menu currency; negative only within the base price (configurable), a configured price never below zero.
Unavailable options cannot be selected (option_unavailable); they are shown as not available or hidden by status.
Historical order safety takes priority over hard deletion: no menu API deletes rows.
Item / category / group / option / image archival is used wherever historical references may exist; archived rows stay out of customer documents.
Cuisine / menu taxonomy remains data-driven; dietary tags are a seeded platform list, not an enum in code.
India veg / non-veg metadata is supported as labels without any food-safety claim; allergen information is the restaurant's free text.
Menu customer visibility is backend-authoritative (MenuAvailabilityService); clients display the answer.
Restaurant menu authorization requires the permission (restaurant.menu.view / .manage) and the location scope of an ACTIVE membership.
Cross-restaurant menu access is prohibited: another restaurant's menu, item, category or image is a 404 with known ids.
Customer, Restaurant and Admin menu resources expose different, closed field sets (MenuPresenter; OpenAPI schemas with additionalProperties false).
Menu cache invalidates after every customer-visible change: catalog_version bumped in the write transaction is the cache key; no explicit flush.
Menu changes carry stale-update protection: version on edits (409 stale_update), menu row lock per write; status switches are last-writer-wins by design.
Cart remains Module 27 (the price quote is stateless; nothing is reserved).
Checkout, taxes, fees and promotions remain Module 29.
Order snapshots (Module 31) will preserve historical prices / configuration; archived menu rows and kept image files make that possible.
One table for variant and modifier groups (menu_option_groups.kind); the kind only tells the apps where to show the group.
The option configuration of an item is replaced as one document (`groups`): ids keep existing groups / options (stable for carts), missing rows are archived.
Duplicate = deep independent copy named "… (copy)" that starts DISABLED; images are copied as new files.
The customer availability merge order is the item's own reason → the restaurant → an unsatisfiable required group; administrators looking at an unpublished menu see MENU_INACTIVE first.

Menu photos are served by the API (GET /api/v1/media/{path}) on the request host so phones reach them through the local proxy; the path pattern is restricted and files are kept when images are archived (local "public" disk until an object-storage decision, CF-331).

The price quote answers 200 with the availability block even when the item cannot be ordered right now; refusals are 422 with issue codes (required, min_selections, max_selections, option_unavailable, unknown_group, unknown_option, duplicate_group, duplicate_option, quantity).
A menu read for a hidden restaurant is a plain 404; a restaurant without an ACTIVE menu answers 200 with menu null; an ACTIVE category without visible items is left out of the customer document.
Archiving a category requires it to be empty (409 category_not_empty).
Administrators read menus only (admin.restaurants.view in the market); a write would need its own permission and audit — not built.
The dashboard's availability choice maps to the backend status: available → ACTIVE, sold out → SOLD_OUT, temporarily unavailable → TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE, unavailable → DISABLED; "archive" is final.
Clients apply search, filters and paging to the published document (reused 30 s) as the fixtures did; the backend decides what the document contains.
Dietary labels are chosen from the backend list in the dashboard (checkboxes, max 6); free text remains only for the development fixtures.
The web HTTP client sends FormData as multipart; uploads happen after the item is saved (the item must exist), removals archive the image.
Laravel 13.33 / PostgreSQL 18 remain in use (spec text says Laravel 12 / PostgreSQL 16 — owner decision CF-268 still open; raised again in the Module 24 report).
Customer profile extends the Module 21 identity (one customers table); no second customer identity record.

Customer phone is read-only on the profile and changes only through OTP verification of the new number (request → code to the new number → verify → uniqueness → update → other sessions revoked → security event).
Customer e-mail is optional and never labelled verified in this module (verification is a later backend requirement, CF-347).
Preferred locale is market- and config-driven (the market's supported_locales; India: en-IN only); the apps show the market options instead of an invented language list.
Favorites reference restaurant locations (a chain is several locations; a customer favors the one they visit); the decision is documented in customer-account-domain.md.
Favorites are idempotent through the unique (customer, location) constraint: 201 when created, 200 when it already was one; remove is 204 either way.
Favoriting is allowed for visible restaurants (open or closed) only; an existing favorite of a restaurant that became hidden is kept and marked unavailable (name only).
Saved locations are journey origin / destination shortcuts, NOT delivery addresses; the API, documents and apps carry journey wording.
Saved locations use PostGIS geography(Point, 4326); market, city and service area are resolved on the server through the Module 22 availability service; a client never sends market or customer ids.
Saved locations may lie outside coverage: they are stored and reported unsupported with the reason; coverage is decided per request, never stored as the answer.
International saved locations are allowed (any country); saving one never creates or activates a market.

Saved location kinds HOME / WORK / OTHER plus a custom label; a configurable limit per customer (20); versions on edits; exactly one default (first saved place; the oldest remaining one is promoted on delete).

Recent locations are kept server-side as explicit selections only: bounded (10), deduplicated by place or rounded coordinates, clearable, pruned after 90 days — never a movement history; clients wire them in Module 26.

Payment methods are references only: the backend never stores or accepts a card number, CVV, expiry entry, UPI PIN, bank password or OTP; provider references are encrypted and never returned; there is no endpoint that accepts payment details.

One default payment method per customer (partial unique index); an expired or unavailable method cannot become the default; remove marks the reference REVOKED and keeps the row for payment history (provider-side revocation is Module 30).
Payment-method statuses ACTIVE / EXPIRED / REVOKED / UNAVAILABLE; EXPIRED is computed from the expiry on read and written back.

Notification preferences are a category × channel matrix (ORDER_UPDATES, PICKUP_UPDATES, PAYMENT_UPDATES, ACCOUNT_SECURITY, PROMOTIONS, PRODUCT_UPDATES × PUSH, SMS, EMAIL, IN_APP) defined in configuration; only cells the customer changed are stored.

Transactional and marketing notices are distinct: security notices are locked on SMS and in-app (cannot be switched off); marketing is off until the customer switches a channel on, which records explicit consent (and withdrawal).
Push-token registration and notification delivery are a later module (Module 33); the preference model is ready.

Sensitive account actions (phone change, deletion request) need recent authentication: a session younger than 30 minutes, or a code to the account's own phone verified on this session within 10 minutes (403 reauthentication_required otherwise).

Account deletion is a recorded request, never a hard delete: the account becomes RESTRICTED (sessions stay), nothing is erased; the erasure / retention behaviour is PENDING FINAL BUSINESS & LEGAL APPROVAL (CF-342).

Privacy and logging: no full phone numbers, codes, tokens, provider references, addresses or coordinates in logs or audit payloads; personal profile fields are audited as "changed" without values; security events carry masked numbers.
All account routes live under /api/v1/customer/... with auth:customer + active; the customer is always the token principal; URL ids of other customers answer 404.

Dedicated closed resources (CustomerProfileResource, FavoriteRestaurantResource, SavedLocationResource, RecentLocationResource, PaymentMethodSummaryResource) and the matrix document; the Module 23 public restaurant resource is reused inside favorites.
No account data is cached; concurrency relies on unique constraints, partial unique indexes for defaults, optimistic versions and row locks.
The Module 21 onboarding route PATCH /auth/customer/profile stays for the sign-up step; the Module 25 profile route is the account editor.

Profile photos are stored under avatars/{customer}/{uuid}.{ext} on the configured disk and served by the existing GET /api/v1/media/{path} (pattern now menu/… or avatars/…); the previous file is deleted on replace / remove (object storage decision shared with CF-331 / CF-349).

A saved location carries a city text field next to locality / region / postal code (the Indian address forms of both apps have one); the formatted line is composed by the client, the backend keeps every field as given.
The customer profile answers the market default locale for an account that has none yet (brand-new customers), never null.
In both apps the account implementation follows the sign-in mode (API sign-in → backend account; mock sign-in → the Module 04 development data): account data only exists for a real session.
The notification inbox (list / mark read) stays development data in both apps until delivery exists, and is labelled so; preferences are real.
Favorites toggle optimistically in the apps and roll back when the backend refuses; the backend answer always wins.
The apps show the local test code in the re-authentication / phone-change dialogs only when the backend says the delivery is "development" (same rule as sign-in).
The Module 04 copy that promised "Cash on Pickup" was removed from both apps: cash at pickup is not an approved payment option.
Coordinates of a saved place can be pasted by the customer until the Maps & Places module provides search and pin-drop (CF-338); the backend tells whether the place is served.
Laravel 13.33 / PostgreSQL 18 remain in use (spec text says Laravel 12 / PostgreSQL 16 — owner decision CF-268 still open; raised again in the Module 25 report).
Driving is the current primary travel mode.
Places and Routing are provider abstractions (PlacesProvider, RoutingProvider) — there is no combined maps service.
Google may be the initial provider, but business logic does not depend directly on Google (one driver class per contract).
Provider credentials remain environment controlled (never in the repository, a log, an error or a response).
PostGIS performs geographic restaurant shortlisting BEFORE detour-provider calls.
Every restaurant is NEVER sent to the Routing Provider: only the bounded shortlist is (guarded in code and by an automated test).
Restaurant location uses PostGIS (geography Point, GiST).
The customer route uses LineString SRID 4326.
The dynamic route search corridor is separate from the configured platform Route Corridors of Module 22.
Spatial proximity is not treated as actual road detour.
Actual detour considers Origin → Restaurant → Destination (minus the base route).
Customer journey results are bounded (candidate cap, page size).
Long routes require bounded / segmented search behaviour (25 km segments, round-robin selection).
Journey ETA is estimated, not guaranteed (always flagged as an estimate; no ready-by promise).
The restaurant's local time zone determines hours at the expected arrival.
Special and overnight hours are considered at arrival.
India remains the current active market.
Cross-border FoodOnTheGo journeys remain future / unapproved (422 cross_border_unsupported).
Journey data is not stored indefinitely by default (30-minute lifetime, pruned after the grace period; no journey history).
Exact route / origin / destination are not routinely logged.
Restaurants do not receive customer origin / destination simply for discovery.
Routing / provider failures do not generate fake results (no fabricated route, ETA or detour; no straight line).
General restaurant browsing remains separate from journey-route availability.
Module 26 does not reserve pickup slots.
Module 26 does not implement turn-by-turn navigation.
Module 27 will consume journey context for Cart.
Module 28 will combine journey ETA with real Pickup Availability.

The development (fake) places and routing providers are refused unless journey.providers.allow_fake is on (default: off in production) — production can never silently plan journeys on synthetic roads; a fake driver there is a MISCONFIGURED failure.

A guest journey is bound to a 256-bit random token returned once, stored as a SHA-256 hash and sent as the X-Journey-Token header; a stranger gets 404 (indistinguishable from "unknown"), the owner of an expired journey gets 410.
A journey lives 30 minutes; expired rows are deleted by journeys:prune after a 60-minute grace period during which the owner is told "expired".
One journey end is given in exactly one form — place id (resolved again on the server), saved place id (coordinates read on the server) or coordinates; two forms at once is a validation error.
Fields a client may never set on a plan (owner, market, provider, route, status, expiry, token) are refused with 422, not ignored.
A restaurant needs an ACTIVE menu to be a journey candidate (journey.eligibility.require_active_menu).
Recommended ordering is a transparent rule: orderable at arrival, open at arrival, shortest actual detour, route order — never a rating (no reviews backend) and never opaque.
A detour depends on the journey and the restaurant only; it is kept per journey for five minutes and reused across filters and corridor widths. FAILED results are never cached.
New detour calculations are limited per journey (12 a minute); reads of calculated results are not.
Only plain arrays are cached (cache.serializable_classes stays false); the test suite runs its cache store with serialization on so a cached PHP object fails in tests.

Only a place the customer searched for and chose becomes a recent place; a device position, a pin and a saved place never do. Places of a live provider are not recorded until its storage terms are confirmed (journey.record_recent_live_places, default off).
Provider health is derived from the platform's own calls (UNKNOWN until one was made); no external health and no monetary cost is claimed.
Clients name the source of every route figure ("development routing model — synthetic roads, not real road data" locally; a provider estimate with a live provider) and show no rating along a journey.
Clients offer only the filters and orderings the API applies (cuisine codes, open at arrival, maximum detour; no "Highest rated").

The route figures of a restaurant on the restaurant page, the cart and the pickup estimate are what the journey's own search said — a restaurant the journey did not find gets none; nothing is estimated in a client.
A guest token is kept by the clients while the backend still answers "expired" to its owner (web: the tab; Android: secure storage, one hour after expiry).
Android asks for the device location through the geolocator plugin only when "Use my current location" is tapped (coarse + fine location declared; no background location).
The maps stay schematic views of the provider's line until a map provider is chosen (CF-060); the note is a caption under the drawing, never an overlay.

Live Google provider verification is BLOCKED / PENDING PROVIDER CONFIGURATION: the adapters are implemented and contract-tested against recorded HTTP shapes; no credentials exist and no live call was made.
Laravel 13.33 / PostgreSQL 18 remain in use (spec text says Laravel 12 / PostgreSQL 16 — owner decision CF-268 still open; raised again in the Module 26 report).
V1 supports one active cart per restaurant location.
Restaurant switching is explicit and never silent.
Guest cart can be claimed/merged after login.
Different-restaurant guest/customer carts cannot merge automatically.
Same item only merges when customization signature matches.
Different customizations remain separate cart lines.
Cart subtotal does not automatically include unapproved tax/fees.
Variants/modifiers are revalidated against current Menu domain.
Sold-out/disabled items are surfaced as cart issues instead of silently disappearing.
Cart mutations support retry/idempotency where needed.
Cart may be linked to Journey Context but can exist without a journey.
Journey expiry does not automatically destroy cart.
Precise journey information is not unnecessarily duplicated into cart.
Restaurant staff do not have access to customer carts.
A guest cart is addressed by a token the SERVER mints and signs (gc1.<issued>.<256 random bits>.<HMAC tag>); only its SHA-256 hash is stored; it travels in the X-Cart-Token header only.
A guest token is stateless until the first item: GET /cart hands one out and creates nothing.
No cart route takes a cart id: a cart is only ever resolved for its owner (session or guest token).
A signed-in customer is the customer: a guest token sent along is ignored except by POST /cart/claim.
PostgreSQL is the store of carts; there is no cart cache and no distributed lock (row lock + version); Redis serves rate limits and event counters only.
Cart statuses are ACTIVE, CONVERTED, EXPIRED, ABANDONED and INVALIDATED with a close reason; CONVERTED is reserved for Module 31 and never deleted by the cleanup.

A guest cart lives 7 days and a customer cart 30 days after its last change; expired carts are closed after a 24-hour grace and closed carts deleted after 30 days (development defaults, configurable).
An expired cart still shows its contents, refuses every change with 410 and is left only by clearing it (or a confirmed switch).
An empty cart stays ACTIVE until it expires and is re-pointed to another restaurant without a question (nothing can be lost).
The cart subtotal is the current price of the lines that can be ordered; a line with a blocking issue is shown but not counted.
A line keeps the price the customer saw only as a snapshot; the price that counts is recalculated from the menu on every read.
Validation is embedded in GET /cart (no separate validate endpoint); POST /cart/refresh is the customer's "update my cart" and accepts changed prices.
Closed right now is information on a cart, not a verdict: pickup time and opening hours are decided in Module 28.
Items may be added while the restaurant is closed or paused (order ahead); the item's own availability is enforced at once.
Adding more of an existing line beyond the item maximum is refused (422 quantity_limit) — never capped quietly; only the sign-in merge caps, and it reports the capped lines.

Sign-in merge policy: no account cart (or an empty / expired one) → the guest cart becomes the customer's; same restaurant → merge by signature; different restaurants → the customer chooses keep_guest or keep_account.
A guest cart is claimed with its token in the customer's session, never with a cart id; the claim spends the token.
The customization signature is sha256(item id | sorted option ids | normalized instructions); an equal configuration keeps the note as first written.
Special instructions are untrusted plain text: cleaned and bounded, kept as written, never interpreted as markup, never a way to change a price.

Cart error codes are lower snake case (Module 20 convention: cart_restaurant_conflict, cart_version_conflict, cart_expired, cart_merge_conflict …); cart issue codes are upper case (PRICE_CHANGED, ITEM_SOLD_OUT …).
An Idempotency-Key on cart changes is optional and scoped to the cart owner and the operation; a request with no identity cannot be scoped and is passed through.
The journey link of a cart is a reference plus labels and figures; a living link is replaced only on the customer's request (PUT /cart/journey).
The cart badge shows the total quantity on the web and on Android.
The web keeps the guest cart token in localStorage (the cart survives a restart); Android keeps it in secure storage.
Android shows the last cart the backend sent while offline, marked as such, and never changes it locally.
The order-level note and the promo field stay on the device until checkout (Module 29).
Administrators see cart COUNTS only (GET /admin/system/carts); nobody but its owner can read a cart.
The development fixture cart belongs to the second fixture customer (Asha); the review account starts with an empty cart.
Laravel 13.33 / PostgreSQL 18 remain in use (spec text says Laravel 12 / PostgreSQL 16 — owner decision CF-268 still open; raised again in the Module 27 report).
Pickup restaurant is derived from Cart.
Restaurant local timezone controls pickup calculations.
India restaurants currently use Asia/Kolkata through configuration.
ASAP means earliest valid pickup, not immediate pickup.
Slot interval is configurable by restaurant/location.
Item preparation metadata may influence estimate.
Preparation time is an estimate, not a guarantee.
Recommended pickup considers both kitchen readiness and traveler arrival.
Customer may select another valid slot where allowed.
Slots outside restaurant hours are never valid.
Frontend slot availability is not a reservation.
A selected slot is not guaranteed until later checkout/order revalidation.
Restaurant settings/hours/status changes trigger pickup revalidation.
Restaurant switch invalidates prior pickup selection.
One active pickup selection per Cart is recommended.
Pickup selection can exist for Guest Cart.
Guest pickup survives authenticated cart claim only if still valid.
Delivery scheduling is not part of Module 28.
Final pickup reservation/order snapshot will occur in later modules.
SELECTED IS NOT RESERVED: Module 28 stores a choice; nothing holds a place until checkout / order creation. PICKUP SLOT HOLD = MODULE 29 / 31.
Required delay = max(preparation estimate + buffer, minimum lead time); the minimum lead is a floor, never an addition.

Preparation estimate = max(restaurant default, slowest item) + a large-order step (10 units free, +5 minutes per started 10, at most +30; development defaults in config/pickup.php) — item times are never summed.
Kitchen-ready time is the server's now plus the delay, rounded up to the minute; no client clock, time zone or timestamp is ever read.
Slots are generated on demand on a grid that counts from the restaurant's local midnight; no slot rows are stored for future times; at most 600 slots per answer.
A slot is offered while start < close and start ≤ close − order cut-off; the first slot of a day may be at the opening instant.
The capacity unit is ORDERS per slot; no configured capacity means no limit; customers see AVAILABLE / LIMITED / FULL and never a count.
LIMITED = something is taken and the last place (or at most 25 % of the capacity) is left.
Capacity is counted from pickup_slot_reservations (FIXTURE / HOLD / ORDER); only local FIXTURE rows exist until checkout and orders are built.
A slot is chosen by a signed, opaque key bound to the restaurant (ps1_<start>_<interval>_<tag>); the format check is anchored.
One pickup selection per cart (unique cart_id, deleted with the cart); statuses SELECTED / STALE / INVALID / EXPIRED / CONVERTED (Module 31).
A selection is judged again on every read; it can become valid again without the customer doing anything (pause ended, place freed).
An ASAP selection follows the clock: its time is the current estimate, not the estimate of the moment it was chosen.
A cart change keeps the selection when the chosen time still fits; when the order now needs longer it is STALE with CART_CHANGED.
The traveller's arrival comes from the cart's journey summary only; it is used while the journey lives and the arrival is not in the past.
Recommendation = first valid option at or after max(kitchen ready, arrival + buffer); basis ARRIVAL or KITCHEN; arrival buffer 0 by default.
The recommendation is guidance: every offered time may be chosen; the answer carries pickup − arrival in seconds.
Pickup endpoints are cart-scoped and take no cart, restaurant or customer id; restaurant, currency, owner, time, status and capacity in a request are refused.
Pickup error codes are lower snake case (slot_full, slot_invalid, pickup_mode_unavailable …); issue codes are upper case (SLOT_FULL, RESTAURANT_CLOSED …).
There is no availability cache and no slot-template cache: every answer is calculated (26 queries, measured).
On a same-restaurant merge at sign-in the guest's pickup time is kept only when the account's cart has none and it still fits; it never crosses restaurants.
The dashboard preview is the customer engine itself for an order with the default preparation time; it warns about settings that offer customers nothing.
Switching both ASAP and scheduled off while pickup stays on is refused; pickup as a whole can be switched off.
Administrators see pickup COUNTS only (GET /admin/system/pickup) and cannot change a restaurant's pickup settings through the restaurant API.
Both clients ask again when the backend's revalidate interval has passed and when they return to the front; the interval is the difference of two backend timestamps.
Android shows pickup times on the backend's wall clock (the UTC offset the backend wrote for each instant).
Without a connection Android shows the last known selection as "Needs connection to confirm availability" and never lets it open checkout.
Neither client ever says a time is "reserved"; both say "selected, not reserved".
Web: VITE_PICKUP_MODE=api; Android: PICKUP_MODE=api; both need the cart on the backend; the mock engines remain for tests only.
Laravel 13.33 / PostgreSQL 18 remain in use (spec text says Laravel 12 / PostgreSQL 16 — owner decision CF-268 still open; raised again in the Module 28 report).
Guest Cart can transition to authenticated Checkout.
Cart is revalidated before Checkout becomes READY.
Frontend grand total is never authoritative.
Payment amount later comes only from Checkout backend.
India Checkout uses INR through Market configuration.
Initial promotion types include fixed/percentage unless expanded explicitly.
Promotion stacking is not enabled unless approved.
No GST percentage is hardcoded as universal India truth.
Tax rules can be version/effective-date aware.
Delivery Fee does not exist in pickup-only V1.
Unapproved platform/service/convenience fees are not shown.
Restaurant commission is not automatically a customer fee.
Customer total, restaurant settlement and FoodOnTheGo revenue are distinct.
Financial rounding uses one backend policy.
Checkout records legal-document versions where applicable.
Final legal wording remains subject to business/legal approval.
Checkout never accepts raw card/CVV/UPI PIN/bank credentials.
Checkout prepares payment; Module 30 executes real payment.
Slot Hold is preferred during payment preparation if safely implemented.
A selected pickup slot is not inherently a reservation.
Module 31 will create immutable Order snapshot.

SLOT HOLD = IMPLEMENTED (Module 29): one place is held in the pickup slot when a checkout is confirmed (READY), with the checkout's expiry; taken atomically under the Module 28 advisory lock; PostgreSQL is the authority.
A checkout is never repaired: when anything it was priced from changes it becomes STALE and a new one is opened, so the customer always sees the new total before paying.
Checkout lifetimes: DRAFT 15 minutes, READY 10 minutes, on the server clock (configurable); a repeated confirmation prolongs nothing.
One live checkout per cart (DRAFT / READY / PAYMENT_PENDING), enforced by the database.
A field the server decides (an amount, a currency, an owner, a status, a time) or a payment credential in a checkout request is REFUSED with 422 — stricter than ignoring it.

Financial calculation order: merchandise subtotal → promotion discount (minimum spend on the pre-discount subtotal) → fees → taxes (after discount unless a rule says before) → total; half-up rounding at the minor unit; inclusive tax split by largest remainder.
No tax rule and no fee rule is seeded for any market. India tax = NOT CONFIGURED until approved rules are supplied (production blocker).

A live promotion (ACTIVE or SCHEDULED) is paused before its discount, scope, currency, code or start can change; DISABLED is final.
Promotion usage = redemptions + uses held by confirmed checkouts; a redemption is counted by the order module, not at checkout.
A customer is told nothing specific about a promotion that is unknown, draft, paused, disabled or not started: all answer "not found".
Promotions are managed by platform administrators only (SUPER_ADMIN writes); restaurant-created promotions are not approved.
A fee code containing DELIVERY or COMMISSION cannot be configured (validation and database CHECK).

VERIFIED (Module 30) = the provider reports a CAPTURED payment on this attempt's own provider order for this attempt's amount and currency. One function writes it (PaymentStateMachine::verify). A client's "success", a valid client signature alone or a webhook's content alone never verifies. VERIFIED is final.

One payment attempt = one provider order; a retry is a new attempt. Development defaults: an attempt lives 15 minutes, at most 5 attempts per checkout, inside a payment window of 45 minutes after confirmation.

Capture: AUTOMATIC, requested per provider order (RAZORPAY_CAPTURE=automatic; "dashboard" leaves it to the account). An authorized payment that is not captured is AUTHORIZED, not paid. To be confirmed against the real Razorpay API once test keys exist (CF-407).

Late success: FAILED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN and REVIEW_REQUIRED can still become VERIFIED — only through reconciliation holding the provider's evidence. A second capture for a checkout that is already paid is REVIEW_REQUIRED (DUPLICATE_PAYMENT), never a silent second payment.
A captured payment for another amount or currency than the attempt's is REVIEW_REQUIRED (PAYMENT_AMOUNT_MISMATCH / PAYMENT_CURRENCY_MISMATCH) and keeps its checkout locked until a person acts.

The fulfilment state is kept apart from the payment state: NOT_APPLICABLE, ORDER_PENDING, RECOVERY_REQUIRED, ORDER_CREATED. A verified payment whose checkout can no longer become an order as it stands is RECOVERY_REQUIRED with the reason.
While a payment is open the checkout's expiry and its pickup-time hold are extended to the attempt's expiry plus 5 minutes; an attempt that ends unpaid gives the checkout back (READY) with its hold.

Provider calls are made outside database transactions; state changes under a row lock (checkout first, then attempt); domain events after commit. There is no outbox: the scheduled sweep is the safety net (CF-414).

Webhooks: the raw body's signature is verified first; events are deduplicated on the provider's event id; a summary of safe fields is stored, never the raw message; the request is answered at once and the work is done on the queue "payments"; handling an event means asking the provider again.
A refused proof of payment (422) makes the backend ask the provider about its own order at once: a real payment is found and verified on the provider's word, an invented one is not there.

There is no fallback provider. PAYMENT_DRIVER is razorpay, fake or empty; with nothing configured payments are unavailable (503) and nothing is simulated. The development provider exists only where APP_ENV is not production. A live key is refused (allow_live = false in code).

A payment request that carries a field the server decides (amount, currency, status, owner, provider, time) or a credential (card number, CVV, UPI PIN, bank password, OTP) is refused as a whole with 422.

Administrators can do exactly one thing to a payment: ask the provider again, with a reason, audited (permission admin.payments.reconcile — SUPER_ADMIN and FINANCE_ADMIN). There is no "mark as paid"; refunds are not available.

Clients keep two references of a payment (checkout id, payment attempt id) and nothing else; after a reload, a restart or a lost connection they ask the backend — also through the checkout when the device kept nothing. No connection is "the status needs confirmation", never "failed".

Razorpay is integrated over plain HTTP on the backend (no SDK), through Razorpay's own checkout.js on the web (loaded only from https://checkout.razorpay.com) and through Razorpay's razorpay_flutter plugin 1.4.7 on Android.
Payment attempts and their timelines are never pruned and outlive their checkout and cart. No raw provider message is kept.
Rate limits per minute: payment start and report 10 per customer, payment status 120, webhooks 600 per address.

Real Orders replace temporary Pickup capacity fixtures.

Checkout becomes CONVERTED after successful Order creation.
Historical Orders do not recalculate from current Menu/Tax/Promotion data.

Paid rejected Order keeps Payment VERIFIED and creates REFUND_REQUIRED state.

An order is created by OrderFulfillmentService in one transaction under the lock of ONE fulfilment row per checkout (order_fulfillments, insert-or-lock): of two workers exactly one creates the order and the other finds it. Triggers: PaymentVerified (queue "orders", after commit), the customer's request for a zero-total checkout, the sweep, an administrator.

At creation the PRICE is not judged again — the customer paid the confirmed price — and the items are not re-validated: an item that became unavailable after payment is the restaurant's rejection (refund REQUIRED), never a repricing. Judged: the payment is VERIFIED for exactly this checkout's total and currency; the checkout is still the one paid; the restaurant is APPROVED and accepting; the market serves customers.

The pickup hold a checkout made becomes the order's reservation (the same row: source ORDER, no expiry). A hold that ran out is re-reserved for the SAME slot under the slot's advisory lock; when no place is left the creation is REVIEW_REQUIRED (ORDER_PICKUP_CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE) and the pickup time is never moved silently.

Order numbers are FOTG-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX: the restaurant-local date of placement and six characters from ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789 (no 0/O/1/I), unique by index and by CHECK, retried on a collision inside a savepoint. A number is never authorization: every lookup is narrowed by who asks (customer, member's locations, admin's markets).

CREATED exists only inside the creating transaction (the database refuses a persisted CREATED); the first state anybody reads is WAITING_FOR_RESTAURANT. PICKED_UP and COMPLETED are in the machine but unreachable before Module 32: the restaurant API has no "picked up" step.

Restaurant steps run under the order's row lock, are idempotent (the same step twice succeeds once and then answers the order as it is, without a second event) and honour expected_version (409 order_version_conflict with current_version and current_status). Rejection takes one of ITEM_UNAVAILABLE, KITCHEN_CAPACITY, CLOSING, TECHNICAL_ISSUE, OTHER plus an internal note the customer never sees.

Money state is kept apart from the status: payment_state PAID | PAYMENT_NOT_REQUIRED (PAID ⇔ a payment reference; NOT_REQUIRED ⇒ total 0) and refund_status NONE … FAILED. Rejecting or cancelling a PAID order sets REQUIRED and writes one order_refunds row for the whole total; REFUNDED is never set in this module. The payment is never touched by the order.

Payment VERIFIED, order NOT CREATED is represented as a fulfilment RETRYING (backoff 30 s · 60 s · 5 min · 15 min · 60 min, swept every minute by orders:recover) or REVIEW_REQUIRED, with the payment RECOVERY_REQUIRED and the reason; administrators list these records and may ask for the creation again (admin.orders.recover, reason, audited) — judged again from scratch, nothing created by hand.

Customers cannot cancel orders in this module. Administrators may cancel with a reason (admin.orders.override, audited); a finished order cannot be cancelled. A new permission admin.orders.recover is held by SUPER_ADMIN, OPERATIONS_ADMIN and SUPPORT_ADMIN.

Pickup credential foundation: a random 32-byte token (only its SHA-256 stored) for the QR payload fotg:pickup:<32 hex>, and a six-character code (same alphabet) stored encrypted with a lookup hash. Shown to the customer while the order is active; revoked on rejection / cancellation; never given to the restaurant or an administrator. Verification is Module 32.

The payment answer carries fulfillment.order_id and order_number. Web and Android keep polling GET /payments/{id} after VERIFIED until the number arrives (RECOVERY_REQUIRED: "payment received, order not confirmed yet, do not pay again"), then open /order-confirmation/{number} — a real order, after it was created; the clients never create, name or invent an order.

Clients map the backend order onto the order model their pages already render (WAITING_FOR_RESTAURANT is shown as "waiting for restaurant"; refund states come from refund_status). Tracking polls the order every 8 s until Module 32's event stream. The dashboard's one "Mark Ready" button takes the two backend steps ACCEPTED → PREPARING → READY_FOR_PICKUP in order.

The restaurant's view of an order carries the customer's name and phone for THIS order, the items and the pickup time — never the payment method, the promotion's economics, the journey or the pickup credential. Administrators see a masked phone, the payment the order recorded, the refunds and the full timeline.

Orders, their lines, timelines and credentials are never deleted; the customer and the restaurant cannot be deleted while they have orders; a deleted checkout, cart or payment leaves the order standing with the public ids as references.
Rate limits per minute: order reads 120 and order steps 60 per identity.

The full-site regression suite keeps the development payment and development orders for its browser (its assertions describe the development order); the backend order path is covered by its own suite. CF-419 stays open until that suite is rewritten for the backend order.
Laravel 13.33 / PostgreSQL 18 remain in use (spec text says Laravel 12 / PostgreSQL 16 — owner decision CF-268 still open; raised again in the Module 31 report).
Realtime transport is not business truth.
Order state changes emit persistent Order events.
Realtime events are sent only after successful commit.
Realtime delivery may be duplicated, missed or reordered.
Client uses Order version/event sequence to prevent state regression.
WebSocket/Reverb is preferred active realtime transport where compatible.
Restaurant Order channels require permission + location scope.
WebSocket outage cannot stop Order operations.
Customer pickup credential is high-entropy and opaque.
Order number alone is not a pickup credential.
Customer phone is not a pickup credential.
Pickup QR contains no customer PII/payment data.
Used pickup QR cannot be replayed.
Manual pickup code is a fallback and receives stronger rate limiting.
Manual code is not derived from Order ID/order number/phone.
Pickup verification requires authorized Restaurant staff.
Customer cannot self-mark Order as picked up.
Concurrent scans produce one logical pickup.
Successful verification transitions Order to PICKED_UP.
PICKED_UP and COMPLETED remain distinct historical states.
V1 may automatically complete after secure pickup verification if no post-pickup process exists.
Completion retry never reactivates consumed pickup credential.
Completed Orders cannot casually return to active preparation states.
Customer precise journey data is not needed for pickup verification.
Restaurant must have backend connectivity for final pickup verification in V1.
OrderCompleted event becomes review-eligibility input for Module 34.

Laravel Reverb is the realtime transport (the spec's preference). Its dependency pin (guzzlehttp/psr7 ^2.6) moved guzzle 8 → 7.15 and psr7 3 → 2.13 and the framework 13.33 → 13.35; accepted after re-running the HTTP-client suites (payments, journeys) on the downgraded client. SSE is not built (optional by the spec).

The broadcast is synchronous after the commit (ShouldBroadcastNow in the after-commit listener) with a 2-second client timeout; a failure is counted and logged, never thrown: no outbox exists (CF-414) and the clients' REST resync is the recovery. One event per channel: the customer's payload (with a message key) and the location's payload (with the item count and the slot) are built once from the committed order.

Every timeline line gets order_events.sequence under the order's row lock (unique per order); the notice carries the version AND the sequence; a client ignores a notice that is not newer on both, reads the order on anything else, and re-reads on reconnect / resume / tab / network. Polling stays as the fallback and the dashboard adds a 60-second safety read even when connected.

Private channels are authorized under /api/v1 with the sanctum guards (customer, restaurant) and the same bearer tokens as the REST API (the web keeps them in sessionStorage, Android in secure storage); the channel callbacks are registered on the signing driver so that tests (null broadcaster) still authorize with the real signature.

The QR secret is stored ENCRYPTED next to its hash (the spec's "secure encrypted snapshot" option): the customer must see the same QR on every visit and device; the hash is the only thing a lookup or a comparison touches. The payload is "FOTG1." + the secret (a format version for later migrations). Module 31 credentials (no secret kept) are rotated on the next customer read.

The manual code is bound to the order (hash of "<order id>:<code>") and the restaurant enters the order number with it, so a code is only ever tried against one order; wrong codes are counted on the credential outside the rolled-back transaction and lock it for 15 minutes after 5; the limits are per staff member (30 / minute), per location (120 / minute) and per order rotation (3 / hour).

Verification is refused as "invalid" (nothing revealed) when the credential cannot be found or belongs to a location the staff member does not reach at all; as "wrong location" (the order's location named) when it is another location of the same organization; the scanner's location must be the order's. There is no administrative "mark picked up" and no customer route touches a pickup.

Completion is automatic right after the verified pickup (V1 has no post-pickup step) but in its OWN transaction: a failure leaves PICKED_UP and the consumed credential, a queued job retries and orders:recover sweeps PICKED_UP orders older than 60 s. Both PICKED_UP and COMPLETED stay on the timeline.

Reverb's allowed origins are host names (it matches the Origin header's host): localhost and 127.0.0.1 locally, never "*"; clients may not publish events; the app key is public to clients by design and excluded from the secret scan, the secret is scanned for.

The dashboard scanner reads the camera with jsQR and also offers a payload field (a hardware scanner types into it) and the manual code; whatever was read is untrusted and sent to the backend as it is. The Android app does not scan (it shows the credential).
A business event (ORDER_READY_FOR_PICKUP) is different from a delivery outcome (PUSH_SENT, PUSH_FAILED): never change an order because a notification failed.
One logical notification per domain event, customer and type; deliveries per channel and per device — never conflicting business notifications per device.
Module 25 preferences (customer_notification_preferences) are reused; no second preference system; no push_enabled column on the customer.

Transactional notices are not all mandatory on every channel: in-app is required, push is the customer's choice, critical security notices may be mandatory, marketing needs explicit consent (never inferred).
The OS notification permission and the FoodOnTheGo preference are separate conditions; both matter for push.
Platform is device metadata (ANDROID); iOS stays deferred (no APNs); web push is a separate future capability.
The installation id is application-generated and random; no IMEI, serial or advertising id is collected.
An FCM token authorises nothing; a shared phone must not keep receiving the previous customer's notices (rebinding on sign-in, unbinding on sign-out).
The ready push never carries the QR secret or the manual code — the customer opens the authenticated app to see them.
Deep links are navigation only (allow-listed targets); the backend still authenticates and authorises the subject.
SENT means the provider accepted the message; DELIVERED only with a trustworthy receipt; the in-app read state is separate.
Retries follow the error category: transient / rate-limited with bounded exponential backoff and jitter, invalid tokens deactivated and never retried, a credential failure never a retry storm.
FCM HTTP v1 (no legacy server-key API); real FCM is not claimed until production credentials, configuration and a build are explicitly tested.
Fake providers are deterministic for tests and local runs and must never pretend to deliver in a production-like environment.

FCM is called over the HTTP v1 REST API with Guzzle and the official google/auth library (service-account OAuth2 token, scope firebase.messaging); the community kreait SDK was not adopted (unofficial, maintenance caveat). The provider maps the documented error codes to INVALID_DESTINATION / TRANSIENT / RATE_LIMITED / AUTH_CONFIGURATION / PERMANENT / UNKNOWN and refuses a payload over 4096 bytes before calling.

Registry (config/notifications.php): order.preparing, order.picked_up and order.completed are in-app only (no push fatigue; the customer is at the counter / done); order.ready is a HIGH-priority PICKUP_UPDATES push on the pickup channel; the Module 30 payment events are not notified separately — the order events carry the outcome; account.phone_changed is a mandatory security notice.

The dedupe key is order public id + event sequence (Module 32) + type (security: the security event id), enforced by a unique index; a concurrent second handler loses the insert and returns the existing row.

IN_APP is a delivery row too (SENT at creation) so one Notification → N deliveries is uniform; a skipped channel is recorded as a SKIPPED delivery with its policy result for diagnostics (a channel the registry says off has no row).

Push targets are the customer's active devices whose reported OS permission is not DENIED; e-mail requires a verified address (no customer verification flow exists yet, so every e-mail is SKIPPED locally); the notification SMS channel is a separate contract from the Module 21 OTP sender and is off locally.

Devices: one ACTIVE row per installation and per token (partial unique indexes); a different customer on the same installation revokes the old row (REBOUND, security event) before creating the new one; the same token on another installation revokes the older holder (TOKEN_REASSIGNED); sign-out revokes (LOGOUT) when the client names its installation in POST /auth/logout or DELETE /customer/devices/current; more than ten active devices retire the oldest (REPLACED); the token is encrypted at rest with a SHA-256 hash for lookup and never leaves the server.

Delivery: one job per delivery on queue "notifications", unique until processing (the retry it dispatches would otherwise be swallowed by its own lock — BUG-228); the send leases the row by conditional UPDATE; backoff 30 s · 2^(n-1) + jitter capped at 900 s, 429 at least 60 s or Retry-After, five attempts; a credential failure pauses the push provider for 300 s; notifications:recover re-queues stranded SENDING rows (lease 120 s), due retries and lost QUEUED rows; notifications:prune applies retention (90 days, 365 for security, attempts 30, revoked tokens purged after 30).

Android: Firebase is initialised only when PUSH_MODE=fcm and the FIREBASE_* client defines exist (FirebaseOptions from the defines, no google-services.json); PUSH_MODE=fake gives a deterministic token so the whole binding / delivery path runs on a machine without a Firebase project — build037 ships fake; notification channels are created natively (orders, pickup, account, offers); the OS permission is asked once per session after sign-in; a foreground push refreshes the inbox and shows a quiet line unless the live screen of that order is open; a tap follows the allow-listed route after sign-in.

Admin: admin.notifications.view (new) for diagnostics / registry, admin.notifications.manage for the audited resend (FAILED with a live destination only), admin.notifications.test (new) for the development / test-only send; GET /admin/system/notifications probes the providers (the fcm driver mints a token; the fake / log providers say so) — never green because configured.

The web header bell shows the backend's unread count; the tracking page re-reads the inbox when the order status changes (the realtime notice of Module 32 is the trigger, the database the authority); the inbox link for a notice is computed from the allow-listed target, never from a URL in the data.
